column2: Knead the flour, egg, salt and water into a firm dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the mince, grated onion and spices.
Roll the dough out very thinly and cut into 2 × 2 cm squares.
Put a piece of filling smaller than a chickpea on each square and pinch the four corners together into a little bundle.
Lightly toast the mantı on a tray in a 200 °C oven for 10 minutes (optional).
Boil in salted water for 10–12 minutes and drain.
Top with garlic yogurt, butter sizzled with chilli flakes, mint and sumac.
Prepared mantı can be frozen on a tray, then bagged and kept for 2 months.
Tulumba (fried syrup pastries)
For the dough: 1.5 cups water
1 tablespoon semolina
1 litre sunflower oil for frying
Boil the syrup for 15 minutes, add lemon and cool.
Boil the water and butter; add the flour and semolina all at once and stir for 3–4 minutes until it comes away from the pan.
Beat the eggs into the cooled dough one at a time.
Put the dough in a piping bag with a star nozzle.
Pipe 5 cm lengths into lukewarm oil (about 130 °C) and cut; fry for 10–12 minutes, gradually turning up the heat.
Drop the fried tulumba into the cold syrup, leave for 5 minutes and remove.
If the oil is too hot at first, the inside stays raw and they won’t puff up.
Şekerpare (syrup-soaked semolina cookies)
125 g butter at room temperature
2 tablespoons semolina
1 sachet vanilla
30 hazelnuts
For the syrup: 2.5 cups sugar
Boil the syrup for 15 minutes, add the lemon and cool.
Beat the butter and icing sugar until creamy, then add the egg.
Add the semolina, vanilla, baking powder and flour and knead into a soft dough that doesn’t stick.
Shape into walnut-sized rounds, press a hazelnut into the centre and arrange on the tray.
Bake in a 180 °C oven for 25–30 minutes until golden underneath.
Pour the cold syrup over the hot cookies and leave until absorbed.
Preparing the ingredients in advance makes cooking easier.
Flour halva
For the syrup: 1.5 cups sugar
Heat the milk, water and sugar until the sugar dissolves; keep hot.
Melt the butter and oil and add the flour.
Toast over a low heat, stirring constantly, for 20–25 minutes until the raw flour smell goes and it turns light brown.
Turn off the heat, carefully add the hot syrup and stir quickly.
Cover and leave to steam for 10 minutes, then shape with a spoon and serve.
Steam rises when you add the syrup; keep your hands away.
Tripe soup (işkembe çorbası)
1 kg cleaned tripe
To serve: 3 garlic cloves, half a cup vinegar, 1 dessert spoon chilli flakes
Wash the tripe several times in cold water; boil in plenty of water in a pressure cooker for 1 hour (2.5 hours in an ordinary pot) until tender.
Remove the tripe and chop finely; strain the cooking liquid.
Toast the flour in butter for 2 minutes, then gradually add the cooking liquid (about 6 cups), stirring until smooth.
Add the chopped tripe, boil for 15 minutes and add salt.
Whisk the egg yolk and lemon, temper with a few ladles of soup, add to the pot and remove from the heat without boiling.
Serve with garlic vinegar and chilli flakes.
The tripe must be thoroughly cooked and cleaned by a trustworthy butcher.
2 days in the fridge; reheat only once.
Beyran soup
600 g lamb on the bone (neck or shank)
1 tablespoon chilli flakes
Boil the meat in plenty of water for 2 hours, skimming off the foam, until it falls off the bone.
Shred the meat, remove the bones and strain the stock.
Wash the rice and half-cook it in a separate pot with a little water.
Put rice, shredded meat and crushed garlic in each bowl.
Salt the boiling stock and ladle it into the bowls.
Sizzle the chilli flakes in butter and drizzle on top.
It is Gaziantep’s breakfast soup; the stock is poured very hot.
Stuffed mussels (midye dolma)
30 large mussels
1 tablespoon pine nuts
1 dessert spoon allspice
1 dessert spoon granulated sugar
Salt, lemon (1 dessert spoon salt)
Scrub the mussel shells with a wire brush and pull off the beards; open them from the side with a knife without separating the shells.
Soak the rice in lukewarm water for 20 minutes and drain.
Soften the onion in olive oil; add the pine nuts, rice and tomato paste and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the spices, currants, sugar, salt and 1 cup hot water and cook until the liquid is absorbed.
Fill the mussels with the stuffing, close them and pack tightly in a pot.
Place an upturned plate on top and add 1.5 cups hot water; cook over a low heat for 25 minutes.
Once cool, serve with lemon.
Before opening, don’t use mussels that aren’t closed or that smell bad.
Steamed sea bass (buğulama)
4 sea bass fillets
2 bay leaves, 1 dessert spoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper
Slice the onion into rings, dice the tomato and slice the pepper into rings.
Put olive oil, onion and garlic in a wide pan and toss for 3 minutes.
Lay the fish on the vegetables and cover with the tomato and pepper.
Add the salt, pepper, bay leaves and lemon slices; pour in half a cup hot water.
Steam, covered, over a low heat for 15–18 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.
Zucchini moussaka
Cut the zucchini into thick rounds.
Soften the onion in oil, add the mince and fry until the liquid evaporates.
Add the tomato paste and diced tomato and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the zucchini and stir, then add the spices and hot water.
Cook covered over a low heat for 25 minutes until the zucchini is tender.
Dalyan köfte (stuffed meatloaf)
600 g mince
1 grated onion
Half a cup boiled peas
3 hard-boiled eggs
Salt, black pepper, cumin (1 dessert spoon salt)
1 tablespoon tomato paste, 1 cup water
Knead the mince, onion, soaked and squeezed bread, raw egg and spices.
Dice the carrot small and boil it with the peas.
Spread the meat mixture into a 1.5 cm-thick rectangle on baking paper.
Put the carrot, peas and the boiled eggs end to end down the middle.
Roll up using the paper, seal the edges and transfer to a baking dish.
Pour the tomato water over and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes; rest, then slice.
Albanian-style liver (Arnavut ciğeri)
500 g calf’s liver
To serve: 1 red onion, half a bunch parsley, 1 dessert spoon sumac
Peel the membrane off the liver, cut into 1.5 cm cubes, rinse in cold water and drain.
Slice the onion thinly and mix with the parsley and sumac.
Toss the liver in flour and spices and shake off the excess flour.
Fry in hot oil for 3–4 minutes until browned outside and cooked through.
Salt after cooking; serve with the onion salad.
Don’t salt the liver and leave it to stand; it toughens.
Hünkâr beğendi (lamb on aubergine purée)
600 g diced lamb
For the beğendi: 4 aubergines
Fry the meat in butter until the liquid evaporates, add the onion and toss for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and grated tomato; add hot water and cook covered for 1–1.5 hours until the meat is tender.
Roast the aubergines over a flame, peel, soak in lemon water and chop finely.
Toast the flour in butter and whisk in the milk; fold in the aubergine and kashar and stir until thick.
Spread the beğendi on the plate, place the meat in the centre and serve.
